chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever divorces [his wife] three times in one session, it is not [considered] three; he who differs [from this], let him return to the Book of Allah. He mentioned the divorce of Ibn Umar, but this narration does not state that he divorced her three times with the obligatory conditions of divorce. It is possible that the intended meaning is if he divorced her while she was menstruating. The report which we have previously mentioned from Abu Basir, the narrator of this hadith, and the detailed hadith of Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz indicate that whoever divorces three times during menstruation, none of them take effect. And if he divorces her during purity, one takes effect, as we have previously mentioned. Taking the detailed hadith is more preferable than the general one. This is also indicated by his saying, 'Then he mentioned the hadith of Ibn Umar,' because Ibn Umar only divorced his wife while she was menstruating. If the intended meaning were what we mentioned, there would be no benefit in mentioning Ibn Umar in this place. And that which indicates that the divorce of Ibn Umar was during menstruation.
ai.seo_question: Does triple divorce in one session count as three or one in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies that a triple divorce pronounced in a single session does not automatically result in three irrevocable divorces, particularly when contextualized with the precedent of Ibn Umar’s divorce during menstruation. The text argues for preferring detailed (mufassal) reports over general ones, suggesting that the three pronouncements may be treated as a single divorce if the requisite conditions (shara'it) are not fully met or if pronounced during the wife's menses. This reflects the Shia juristic preference for retaining the possibility of reconciliation in such cases, contrasting with the Sunni view of immediate triple irrevocability.
